 India U-17 Team Eye Crucial Win Against Palestine to Strengthen Qualification Hopes

 Kuala Lumpur, November 17 (H.S.): The Indian U-17 men's football team will face its toughest challenge yet when it takes on Palestine on Tuesday in the AFC U-17 Asian Cup Uzbekistan 2027 Qualifiers. Both teams head into the Group E encounter after winning their opening two matches, making this fixture crucial in the race for the top spot and qualification for the continental tournament.
 According to the All India Football Federation (AIFF), India began its campaign with a 4-2 victory over Singapore before registering an emphatic 12-0 win against Guam. Palestine, meanwhile, defeated hosts Malaysia 2-0 and secured a 5-0 victory over Guam.
 Both teams have accumulated six points from two matches, but India currently lead Group E on a superior goal difference. India have a goal difference of plus 14, while Palestine are second with plus seven. Since head-to-head results are the first tiebreaker when teams finish level on points, Tuesday's encounter could play a decisive role in determining the group leaders and the team that advances to the next stage. Only the group winners will qualify for the final tournament.
 The upcoming fixture will mark the fourth meeting between India and Palestine in AFC youth competitions. Both sides have registered one victory each, while their other encounter ended in a draw. Palestine defeated India 1-0 in the 2016 AFC U-19 Championship Qualifiers, while India secured a 3-0 win in the 2018 AFC U-16 Championship Qualifiers. Their most recent meeting took place in Ahmedabad last November during the previous edition of the AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers, where the match ended in a 1-1 draw.
 India head coach Mehrajuddin Wadoo is aware of the challenge posed by Palestine but has made it clear that his team intends to dictate the game by relying on its own strengths and playing style.
 “Palestine are a competitive side, and we expect them to provide a different kind of challenge. We will respect Palestine, but at the same time, we want to play our own brand of football and impose our style on the game,” he said.
 India have scored 16 goals in their first two matches, making their attacking performance one of the standout features of the campaign so far. Wadoo said the team's preparations were beginning to translate into results on the field.
 “Scoring 16 goals in two matches is a positive sign and reflects the hard work we have put in. Our work on attacking patterns, movement and understanding in the final third is beginning to show, but we must remember that this is only the beginning,” he said.
 Several players have contributed to India's goal-scoring exploits in the tournament. Dallalmuon Gangte has scored consecutive hat-tricks in the team's opening two matches, while Raj Singh Wahengbam produced an outstanding performance against Guam, scoring four goals. Wadoo expressed satisfaction with the collective contribution of the squad.
 “It is extremely encouraging to see different players take responsibility and contribute to the team's success. What matters most to me is that we are not dependent on one or two individuals. We want to develop a team where every player understands their responsibility, whether it is scoring goals, creating opportunities or contributing defensively,” he said.
 The coach also emphasised that healthy competition within the squad was essential for the players' development. While the team's opening results have been encouraging, he believes there are still several areas that need improvement.
 “We need to be more consistent with our decision-making, improve our defensive organisation and maintain concentration throughout the 90 minutes. The most important thing is that the boys are showing the right mentality, discipline and desire to represent the country. We respect every opponent, and our focus now is entirely on preparing well for Palestine,” Wadoo said.
 Having secured two consecutive victories, India have an opportunity to consolidate their position at the top of Group E and take a significant step towards qualifying for the AFC U-17 Asian Cup 2027. Following the Palestine encounter, India will play their final group-stage match against hosts Malaysia on November 20.
